title: Some Nutso Fan Theories
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant swap TV fan theories, defining a fan theory as one that must hold up across the show's circumstances. They cover Murder, She Wrote as a serial-killer theory, the Saved by the Bell theory that the show is Zack Morris's daydream (with its origin traced to a 2012 Cracked post by Logan Trent), The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air as a post-death afterlife, Gilligan's Island as Hell and the Seven Deadly Sins, Star Trek and Sherlock Holmes, Andy Griffith's Mayberry as the post-apocalyptic Star Trek episode "Miri," filming locations for Mash, Garfield's six bleak strips as a dying cat's hallucination, Breaking Bad's blue meth causing The Walking Dead outbreak, The Flintstones and The Jetsons as a post-apocalyptic future, Scooby-Doo set after an economic collapse, St. Elsewhere as taking place in autistic Tommy Westfall's imagination (the "Tommy Westfall universe"). The episode closes with listener mail about a hidden Canadian Club whiskey cache near Lake Placid.

segments.title: Opening banter and defining fan theories
segments.summary: Hosts joke about Jerry's existence and introduce the episode on TV fan theories. They define a fan theory as an idea that must hold up across a show's circumstances, contrasting Murder, She Wrote's serial-killer theory as weak but arguable.

segments.title: Saved by the Bell daydream theory
segments.summary: The hosts describe the theory that Saved by the Bell is Zack Morris's daydream, traced to a 2012 Cracked post by Logan Trent. They cover the predecessor Good Morning, Miss Bliss, the changed character, and theme song lyrics as evidence.
topics: Saved by the Bell fan theory

segments.title: The Fresh Prince is dead and Gilligan's Island as Hell
segments.summary: The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air is theorized to be an afterlife story after Will's death. The hosts then cover a drug-deal theory for Gilligan's Island, dismissed, and the better theory that the island is Hell with characters as the Seven Deadly Sins, which Sherwood Schwartz reportedly confirmed.
topics: The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air dead theory
Gilligan's Island Seven Deadly Sins theory

segments.title: Star Trek connections: Spock, Mayberry, and Mash
segments.summary: A theory that Spock is related to Sherlock Holmes, based on a quote from The Undiscovered Country. Then the Star Trek episode Miri set in a post-apocalyptic Mayberry using the Andy Griffith back lot, and filming locations for Mash in the Hollywood Hills and California.
topics: Andy Griffith Show Star Trek Miri connection

segments.title: Garfield's six strips as a dying cat's hallucination
segments.summary: The October six-strip Garfield sequence where Garfield is alone in an abandoned house is theorized to be the hallucination of a dying starving cat. Jim Davis reportedly laughed at the idea. The hosts mention the animated short Allegro non troppo and Garfield Without Garfield.

segments.title: Breaking Bad blue meth and The Walking Dead outbreak
segments.summary: Theory that blue meth from Breaking Bad caused the zombie outbreak in The Walking Dead, citing Glenn's red Dodge Challenger, a dealership manager named Glen, a bag of drugs in season two, and Merle's description of his supplier.
topics: Breaking Bad Walking Dead blue meth theory

segments.title: The Flintstones and The Jetsons as post-apocalyptic future
segments.summary: Theory that The Flintstones is set in a post-apocalyptic future, with anachronisms such as record players, Christmas, and talking animals. The Jetsons' class divide between the clouds and the Small Line is discussed, along with a movie line about grass that undermines the theory.

segments.title: Scooby-Doo set after economic collapse
segments.summary: Theory that Scooby-Doo takes place after a world economic collapse: abandoned places, squatting villains with advanced skills and PhDs who turn to monetary crimes. The hosts note the empty settings.

segments.title: St. Elsewhere and the Tommy Westfall universe
segments.summary: The ending of St. Elsewhere reveals the show was a snow globe held by autistic boy Tommy Westfall, leading to the theory that the show took place in his mind. Dwayne McDuffie's 2002 post and a chain of crossovers (Cheers, Frasier, Star Trek, Angel, Firefly, Red Dwarf, Doctor Who, John Munch) extend it to hundreds of shows.

segments.title: Hidden Canadian Club whiskey
segments.summary: Listener Chris Orlaff writes about his mother's search for a Canadian Club whiskey bottle from the eighties promotion, reportedly hidden near Lake Placid, New York. Clues were studied and searched but the bottle was not found.

segments.title: Closing and contact information
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to share Mother's Day stories and fan theories via Twitter, Facebook, email, and the website, then sign off.
